claims.text: TC4 (Ti-6Al-4V) is an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase titanium alloy.
TC4 has low surface hardness and poor wear resistance under extreme-service conditions.
TC4 has low density and high specific strength.
Corrosion resistance is an inherent beneficial property of TC4 that should be preserved.
The proposed intervention is laser cladding a refractory high-entropy-alloy coating containing a controlled fraction of pre-dispersed WC particles onto TC4.
The intervention will produce a homogeneous refractory HEA matrix with uniformly distributed fine WC-derived carbide particles.
The intervention will produce a compositionally graded, metallurgically bonded interface with TC4.
Controlling laser power, scanning speed, and preheating will minimize dilution.
Normal loads of 10–30 N represent extreme high-contact-stress service for the proposed system.
High mixing entropy and controlled laser cladding promote formation of a dense, uniform, metastable refractory HEA coating.
A laser-clad multi-principal-alloy coating on TC4 can improve wear resistance through solid-solution formation and coating-structure changes.
The proposed refractory HEA coating will maintain corrosion resistance.
WC-derived carbide particles will provide dispersion strengthening and arrest plastic deformation and abrasive wear.
A graded interfacial zone will minimize residual stresses.
The combined HEA matrix, carbide reinforcement, and graded interface will enhance hardness and reduce wear during severe contact loading.
The coated surface will have at least 1.5 times the microhardness of untreated TC4.
The coated surface will have a significantly lower wear rate than untreated TC4 under high-contact-stress conditions.
The coated surface will have a significantly lower friction coefficient than untreated TC4 under high-contact-stress conditions.
The coating will improve surface performance without compromising TC4's lightweight character, strength, or corrosion resistance.

Failure to achieve a statistically significant hardness increase of at least 1.5 times, together with clearly reduced wear rate and friction coefficient relative to both controls, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The design specifies only two sample sets, with the second set being either untreated TC4 or a baseline HEA-coated control, but the falsification rule requires comparison against both untreated TC4 and the baseline HEA-coated samples. Three distinct groups would be needed to execute that rule.
